intro: Week 7 opened in Paris and rolls on with the Chiefs still unbeaten and headed to Seattle tonight. The Colts have a new front office order after firing Chris Ballard, and the Rams lost Davante Adams to a ruptured hamstring. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after 2-4 start
top.dek: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made the move one day after a 26-20 home loss to the Titans, who had not won all season. Indianapolis blew a 13-0 halftime lead. Assistant GM Ed Dodds now runs personnel and coach Shane Steichen stays.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Rams lose Davante Adams to a ruptured hamstring
top.dek: Adams went down in the final minute against Arizona and could miss six to 10 weeks. Kobie Turner is headed to injured reserve and nose tackle Poona Ford is out for the year. Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie are questionable today.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Chad Ryland hits six of six, wins it for Arizona
top.dek: The Cardinals kicker made all six field goal tries in an 18-16 win at the Rams, from 34, 30, 22, 38, 27 and 43 yards. He scored every Arizona point, and the 43-yarder won it as time expired. The league named him NFC Special Teams Player of the Week.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 309.8: Bryce Young's passing yards per game, tops in the NFL
top.dek: Carolina averages 404.4 yards a game, second in the league after ranking 27th last year. The Panthers lead the NFC South at 3-2 and host 1-5 Tampa Bay today. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik now calls the plays.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs visit the Seahawks on Sunday night
top.dek: Kansas City is 5-0 and the lone unbeaten team left in the AFC. Kickoff at Lumen Field is 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch Seattle's pass protection, the status of Drew Lock's elbow and how the Chiefs cover their injuries.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit the bye at 5-1 minus a safety

stories.text: Bills survive Vegas, then lose Gardner-Johnson for a game
stories.summary: Buffalo held off the Raiders 33-30 on Oct. 18 and went into the bye at 5-1. Josh Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns, and Khalil Shakir recovered a botched drop-kick onside try to end it. The win came with a cost: the league suspended safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson one game for spitting at Raiders players after his ejection.

stories.text: Moore and Oliver stayed out, with the bye as the reason
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) and defensive tackle Ed Oliver (knee) missed a second straight game against the Raiders. Coach Joe Brady said both were close, but the team played it safe with the bye coming. Brady hopes both are back for the Nov. 1 game against Baltimore.

stories.text: Igbinosun earns the boundary corner job
stories.summary: Rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun broke up three passes against Las Vegas, tied for third among all Buffalo defenders that day. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said he has earned a high majority of the snaps at boundary corner. Leonhard's praise matters more with Gardner-Johnson headed for a suspension.

stories.text: 3: points separating Buffalo from two straight opponents
stories.summary: The Bills have won back-to-back games by three points, 37-34 in overtime over the Rams and 33-30 at Las Vegas. Allen was 23 of 33 for 255 yards against the Raiders, and Tyler Bass made all four field goals. Buffalo went 3 of 5 in the red zone.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Baltimore on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Buffalo is off this week. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET against the 4-2 Ravens at Highmark Stadium. Gardner-Johnson is in line to miss that one unless he wins an appeal, and Moore and Oliver are the returns to watch.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins try to find a first lead at MetLife

stories.text: Winless Miami hits the road for a Jets game it needs
stories.summary: The Dolphins come off the bye at 0-5 with the league's worst point differential, minus 62. They have not led at any point this season. Sunday at MetLife gives them their best look at a first win against a 2-4 Jets team.

stories.text: Louis returns from IR; Beal doubtful again
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Louis, out since the opener with a knee injury, was activated and listed questionable after a full Friday practice. Edge rusher Rob Beal Jr. (hamstring) is doubtful and appears headed for a fourth straight miss, and cornerback Reese Taylor (quad) is out. Receiver Caleb Douglas came off the report after full practice.

stories.text: Ollie Gordon II is the one thing working in Miami
stories.summary: Running back Ollie Gordon II has 188 rushing yards and two touchdowns over his last two games. He is the bright spot in an offense that scored a season-high 24 points in a loss to Cincinnati. Quarterback Malik Willis has 849 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions.

stories.text: 76.0: the completion rate Miami is allowing
stories.summary: Opponents are completing 76.0 percent of their passes against Miami, a pace that would break the record of 72.7 set by the 2016 Lions. The Dolphins also have only four sacks through five games, their lowest total since at least 1981.

stories.text: At the Jets today, then New England on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Miami plays at the Jets today at 1 p.m. ET on CBS from MetLife Stadium. Next up is a home game against New England on Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, per the Patriots' schedule release. Watch whether Miami finally leads at any point today.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Pats fall to Bears 30-24, banged up on the line

stories.text: Bears hold off Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
stories.summary: New England dropped to 4-3 after Chicago kicked a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left and then recovered the Patriots' onside kick. The Bears led 20-7 at the half. The Patriots' three-game winning streak ended.

stories.text: Doubs lands on IR as the line thins out
stories.summary: Receiver Romeo Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and will miss at least four games. He is the third Patriots wideout on IR this season. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown were ruled out for the Bears game, along with cornerbacks Carlton Davis, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty.

stories.text: Maye throws for 321 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Drake Maye went 24 of 31 for 321 yards and two touchdowns and added a 7-yard rushing score. Rhamondre Stevenson caught five passes for 93 yards, including a 48-yard touchdown on the last play of the third quarter. Maye's only interception came in the end zone late in the second quarter.

stories.text: 3: Patriots wide receivers now on injured reserve
stories.summary: Doubs joins A.J. Brown (Week 1) and Mack Hollins (Week 4) on IR. Only four receivers remain on the 53-man roster: A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams. Doubs had 14 catches for 261 yards and three touchdowns through six weeks.

stories.text: At Miami on Nov. 1 against a winless team
stories.summary: Per the team's schedule release, New England visits the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. Miami is 0-5 as of today. Watch how a thin receiver room and a hurt interior line handle the trip.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets host winless Miami with Hall questionable

stories.text: Jets cannot afford to slip against a winless Dolphins team
stories.summary: New York is 2-4 after a 26-19 loss at New England in which it trailed 17-3 at the half. The Jets host 0-5 Miami today and are home favorites. One local preview called it a game the Jets should win if they want to keep their season alive.

stories.text: Hall and Parham questionable, three Jets out
stories.summary: Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and lineman Max Mitchell (concussion) are out. Running back Breece Hall (quad) and left guard Dylan Parham (knee) are questionable. Receiver Adonai Mitchell (broken finger) was expected to play on the final report, though an earlier report listed him doubtful.

stories.text: Omar Cooper Jr. scores his first NFL touchdown
stories.summary: The rookie receiver came back from an ankle sprain that kept him out since Week 1. He caught six passes for 103 yards in New England, including a 48-yard touchdown. Geno Smith went 20 of 30 for 252 yards in the same game.

stories.text: 1,336: Geno Smith's passing yards through six games
stories.summary: Smith has completed 122 of 177 passes for 1,336 yards and seven touchdowns with one interception. His one pick came in the loss at New England. He faces a Miami defense allowing a 76 percent completion rate.

stories.text: Dolphins at MetLife today, 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: The Jets host Miami today at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at MetLife Stadium. Watch the second half: New York outscored New England 16-9 after halftime last week but dug the early hole. Hall's status decides how much Braelon Allen carries.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens wait on Lamar Jackson's ankle

stories.text: Ravens let a 10-0 lead slip, and Lamar Jackson's ankle is the question
stories.summary: Baltimore scored on its first two drives at Cleveland and never scored again, falling 13-10 on a last-snap field goal. Tyler Huntley started for the second straight game while Jackson sat. Jackson is back in practice and carries a questionable tag into Sunday's game against Cincinnati.

stories.text: Ravens list Jackson questionable, Robinson and Hawkins out
stories.summary: Jackson (ankle) was limited all three days and is questionable. Outside linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) are out, and cornerback T.J. Tampa Jr. (knee) is doubtful. Tackle Ronnie Stanley did not practice Friday after leaving the Browns game late.

stories.text: Derrick Henry keeps leading the league in carries
stories.summary: Henry has 130 carries, the most in the NFL, for 534 yards and 7 touchdowns, tied for the league lead. His lost fumble against Cleveland led to the tying touchdown, a rare blemish. Zay Flowers leads all pass catchers with 50 or more routes at 3.8 yards per route run.

stories.text: 235: the yards Baltimore gained in Cleveland
stories.summary: That total was nearly even with the Browns' 237 net yards, and the Ravens went scoreless after the first quarter. Baltimore had a 10-0 halftime lead and lost the time of possession battle 31:53 to 28:07. The offense averages 26.0 points per game, seventh in the league.

stories.text: Bengals visit M&T Bank Stadium today
stories.summary: Baltimore hosts Cincinnati at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the quarterback decision first, then whether Trey Hendrickson, 25 pressures against his old team, can reach Joe Burrow. Hendrickson has a 22.7 percent pressure rate, third among edge rushers.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals come off the bye for Baltimore

stories.text: Bengals use the bye to fix late-game habits
stories.summary: Coach Zac Taylor said penalties and wasted field position need cleaning up after Cincinnati nearly gave away a 28-10 fourth-quarter lead in Miami. He called the issues fixable. The Bengals visit Baltimore today with a chance to climb to 4-2.

stories.text: Bengals report no game designations, with line rest days
stories.summary: Cincinnati's Friday report lists no game status for anyone. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) went full Thursday and Friday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, Dexter Lawrence II and B.J. Hill sat out Friday for rest. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm) and tight end Tanner Hudson are on injured reserve. One outlet still listed Dugger as questionable.

stories.text: Joe Burrow threw four touchdowns without a sack
stories.summary: In the 31-24 win at Miami on Oct. 11, Burrow went 23 of 32 for 190 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions. The Dolphins never sacked him. Ja'Marr Chase caught six passes for 77 yards, including a 45-yard score.

stories.text: 22: straight field goals for Evan McPherson
stories.summary: McPherson's 26-yarder against Miami was his 22nd consecutive make, a Bengals record. The streak goes into a road game where points have come hard for both sides. Cincinnati's offense also ran for 119 yards in that win.

stories.text: At Baltimore, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Bengals play the Ravens today at M&T Bank Stadium. Cornerback DJ Turner II held Zay Flowers to one catch for 14 yards last year, and Flowers now tops the league in yards per route run. Lamar Jackson is questionable, so Tyler Huntley may start.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns own first place in the North

stories.text: Browns beat Baltimore on the last snap to take the division lead
stories.summary: Cleveland rallied from a 10-0 deficit for a 13-10 win on Andre Szmyt's 37-yard field goal as time expired. The Browns are 4-2 and first in the AFC North, with division wins over Pittsburgh and Baltimore. Carson Schwesinger's forced fumble on Derrick Henry set up the tying drive.

stories.text: Delpit and Ward questionable, Gabriel out again
stories.summary: Safety Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder), cornerback Denzel Ward (hand), linebacker Quincy Williams (neck) and running back Dylan Sampson (knee) are questionable at Tennessee. Quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back) is out for a third straight game despite full practice. Guard Teven Jenkins and defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr. and Kalia Davis are also out.

stories.text: Andre Szmyt has two game-winners already
stories.summary: Szmyt hit the winner against Pittsburgh in Week 4 and again against Baltimore as time ran out. He made both of his attempts Sunday, the 37-yarder after Deshaun Watson led a 10-play, 62-yard drive. Watson finished 16 of 26 for 164 yards and was sacked five times.

stories.text: 4: late go-ahead drives this season
stories.summary: The Week 6 march was Cleveland's fourth fourth-quarter go-ahead drive of the year. The offense went 4-for-10 on third down in the second half after going 1-for-6 before the break. The defense held Baltimore to a season-low 235 net yards.

stories.text: At Tennessee, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Browns visit the 1-5 Titans at Nissan Stadium today. Cleveland averages 17.7 points per game, 28th in the league, but has allowed one rushing touchdown all year. Pittsburgh comes to town next week for the rematch.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers chase the first NFL win in France

stories.text: Steelers play the league's first Paris game despite street protests
stories.summary: Pittsburgh and New Orleans meet at Stade de France at 9:30 a.m. ET. The NFL kept the game on after civil unrest in France, and Aaron Rodgers said the league would cancel it if conditions turned unsafe. The Steelers flew in early Friday and lost their first practice to weather.

stories.text: Dowdle questionable, Watt and Ramsey full by Friday
stories.summary: Running back Rico Dowdle (knee) was limited all week and is questionable. T.J. Watt (calf), Alex Highsmith (groin) and Jalen Ramsey (wrist) were full participants Friday. Cornerback Brandin Echols and receiver Ben Skowronek were ruled out. Safety DeShon Elliott came off injured reserve; sources differ on whether he is probable or questionable.

stories.text: Aaron Rodgers is tied for third all time in touchdown passes
stories.summary: Rodgers has 539 career touchdown passes and 12 this season with 1,487 yards. Over the last two games he has completed 68.8 percent of his throws for five touchdowns and one interception, including a six-yard overtime score to rookie Germie Bernard against Tampa Bay.

stories.text: 10: takeaways for a zone-heavy Pittsburgh defense
stories.summary: The Steelers have 10 takeaways, tied for third in the league. They play zone on 82.8 percent of dropbacks, and five of their six interceptions came against it. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions against zone, tied for second most.

stories.text: Saints in Paris, then Browns in Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Kickoff is 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network, with the Steelers favored by 2.5. Watch the Saints' run defense, which ranks 30th in yards allowed and 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed. Cleveland visits Pittsburgh in Week 8, the rematch of the Browns' Week 4 win.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans ride Fairbairn's kick into Giants game

stories.text: Fairbairn's 49-yarder beats Jaguars in London
stories.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired to give Houston a 34-31 win over Jacksonville at Wembley. The Texans answered a Cam Little 60-yarder that had tied it at 31. Houston now sits two games behind the Jaguars in the AFC South with a chance to climb back today.

stories.text: Four Texans ruled out against the Giants
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin), tackle Blake Fisher (thumb), and safeties Reed Blankenship (concussion and hand) and Jalen Pitre (shoulder) are all out for today's game. That thins the backfield and the secondary at the same time. Wideout Tank Dell is back on the active roster.

stories.text: Stroud leads the league in volume after Jacksonville
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud went 24 of 34 for 312 yards and three touchdowns against the Jaguars and drove the 36-yard winning series, his eighth game-winning drive. Through six games he has 1,714 yards on 143 of 219 passing with nine touchdowns and one interception. Those yards rank second in the NFL.

stories.text: 673: Days between Tank Dell's NFL snaps
stories.summary: Dell returns today for his first NFL game in 673 days. He caught 98 passes for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns in 25 games after Houston took him 69th overall in 2023. Marvin Harrison Jr. made his Texans debut last week, so the receiver room is deeper than it has been all year.

stories.text: Giants visit Houston at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Giants come to NRG Stadium today, with JJ McCarthy making his first start for New York. Houston is a 10.5-point favorite. Watch whether the Texans can run without Montgomery and protect Stroud without Fisher.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts fire Ballard, face unbeaten Vikings

stories.text: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after 2-4 start
stories.summary: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon fired Ballard on Monday, one day after a 26-20 home loss to the winless Titans in which Indianapolis gave up a 13-0 halftime lead. Ballard went 72-82-1 in 10 seasons and the Colts have missed the playoffs since 2020. Assistant GM Ed Dodds oversees personnel for now, and coach Shane Steichen stays in place.

stories.text: Gardner, Warren among four Colts out in Minnesota
stories.summary: Cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf), tight end Tyler Warren (groin), linebacker CJ Allen (ankle) and receiver Anthony Gould (concussion) are out. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and cornerback Justin Walley (knee) are questionable. Losing Gardner and Warren hurts both sides of the ball against an unbeaten Vikings team.

stories.text: Taylor posts season-high 151 scrimmage yards in loss
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor ran 21 times for 94 yards and a touchdown against Tennessee and caught two passes for 57 more. He also lost a fumble, his second of the year. He has seven total touchdowns, but his 4.0 yards per carry would be a career low.

stories.text: 6: Sacks Daniel Jones took against Tennessee
stories.summary: Jones went down six times and took 11 hits in the loss to the Titans. Minnesota blitzes often under defensive coordinator Brian Flores, so protection is the first thing to watch today. The Colts have no cushion up front or on the schedule.

stories.text: At Minnesota at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, then Jacksonville
stories.summary: The Colts face the unbeaten Vikings today at U.S. Bank Stadium, then travel to Jacksonville on November 1. Steichen faces Flores' pressure packages with a short-handed secondary. The front office search for a new GM runs in the background.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars regroup on bye after Wembley heartbreak

stories.text: Coen stands by 60-yard try in London loss
stories.summary: Jacksonville lost 34-31 to Houston when Cam Little's 60-yarder tied it and Fairbairn answered with a 49-yard kick as time ran out. Liam Coen defended kicking on fourth-and-4 instead of going for it, and called the 114 rushing yards allowed humbling. The Jaguars are 4-2 and open this week on a bye.

stories.text: Secondary thin heading into the bye
stories.summary: Cornerback Buster Brown is working through a hamstring injury, Montaric Brown has missed a couple of games, and the team has had trouble at safety. The bye gives Jacksonville time to heal before the Colts arrive November 1. No team injury designations apply this week.

stories.text: Lawrence throws for four scores in defeat
stories.summary: Trevor Lawrence went 24 of 41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception against Houston. The offense piled up 412 yards and 24 first downs. Lawrence has 14 touchdowns against four picks through six games, and Coen says he has been very pleased with him.

stories.text: 17-6: Jaguars record in the Coen era
stories.summary: Jacksonville is 17-6 through 23 games under Coen and third in the AFC behind Kansas City (5-0) and Buffalo (5-1). Two of the three losses this year came by one score. Local writers see the pass rush, with Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen quiet since Week 1, as the fix to find.

stories.text: Bye week, then Colts at home November 1
stories.summary: Jacksonville is off today. The next game is Sunday, November 1 at home against Indianapolis. Kickoff time and network were not confirmed in the sources reviewed. Expect questions about Brian Thomas Jr., who dropped two first-half passes against Houston and sat the second half.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans chase back-to-back wins against Browns

stories.text: Titans get Saleh his first win, beat Colts 26-20
stories.summary: Tennessee erased a 13-0 halftime deficit in Indianapolis for its first win of the season and the franchise's 500th all-time. Robert Saleh earned his first victory as head coach. Cam Ward led a seven-play, 52-yard drive for the winning points.

stories.text: Ridley, Spears, two safeties questionable vs. Browns
stories.summary: Receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) did not practice Thursday or Friday and is questionable. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), safety Tony Adams (ankle) and safety Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) carry the same tag. Linebacker Dorian Mausi (foot) practiced fully, though the NFL.com report lists him as out, so the sources disagree.

stories.text: Simmons wrecks the Colts with two sacks and a strip
stories.summary: Jeffery Simmons recorded six tackles, two sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in Indianapolis. He moved to 46.5 career sacks, passing Ted Washington for 10th on the franchise list. Jermaine Johnson II added two sacks as well.

stories.text: 6: Sacks by the Titans, none allowed
stories.summary: Tennessee sacked the Colts six times and did not give up one. The defense also took the ball away three times and blocked a punt that Oluwafemi Oladejo returned for a touchdown. Cam Ward finished only 11 of 22 for 102 yards, so the defense carried the day.

stories.text: Browns visit Nashville at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Tennessee hosts Cleveland today, with the Browns listing quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back) out and cornerback Denzel Ward (hand) questionable. The Browns are 2.5-point favorites. The Titans want a second straight win after a 1-5 start.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos survive Seattle in overtime, now to Arizona

stories.text: Broncos escape Seattle 17-14 in overtime
stories.summary: Denver improved to 4-2 on Thursday night when Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard field goal in overtime. Seattle erased a late deficit with a touchdown and two-point conversion, then tied it with a field goal after Denver failed to run out the clock. Sam Darnold threw two interceptions, one late in regulation and one on Seattle's first overtime drive.

stories.text: Surtain and Coleman questionable at Arizona
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) carry questionable tags for the Cardinals game. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and running back Tyler Badie (thumb) are out. Riley Moss and Jaylen Waddle practiced fully and carry no designation.

stories.text: Lutz and Abrams-Draine close out Seattle
stories.summary: Kicker Wil Lutz hit the 53-yarder that ended it, and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine picked off Darnold with under 1:30 left in regulation to keep Denver in front. J.K. Dobbins ran 17 times for 41 yards and a score, and R.J. Harvey added a touchdown on six carries.

stories.text: 107: Bo Nix's passing yards in the win
stories.summary: Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions against Seattle, and added 2 yards on four carries. The Broncos still won, but coach Sean Payton called the second half a struggle for the offense.

stories.text: At Arizona, Sunday 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver travels to face the Cardinals, who list running back Jeremiyah Love out with an ankle injury. Watch whether the Broncos get Surtain on the field and whether the offense finds a rhythm after a quiet showing last Thursday.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs head to Seattle on Sunday night

stories.text: Unbeaten Chiefs face champion Seahawks tonight
stories.summary: Kansas City is 5-0 and the only undefeated AFC team as it visits Seattle on Sunday Night Football. The Seahawks, defending Super Bowl champions, have lost two straight, including a 17-14 overtime loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes has played in Seattle once before, a 38-31 loss in December 2018.

stories.text: Rice, Moore and Smith out in Seattle
stories.summary: The Chiefs ruled out receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), running back Brashard Smith (hamstring) and lineman Jaylon Moore (concussion) for tonight. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) is questionable. Moore left the Chargers game in the second quarter with the concussion.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker runs wild in return to Seattle
stories.summary: Walker ran for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the 22-6 win over the Chargers, including a 33-yarder. The former Seahawk leads the league with 665 rushing yards and now faces his old team.

stories.text: 100: Mahomes' career wins after beating LA
stories.summary: Mahomes threw for 272 yards in the win over the Chargers, his 100th career victory. Xavier Worthy caught seven passes for 73 yards and Travis Kelce added five for 53.

stories.text: At Seattle, Sunday 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: The Chiefs play tonight in Seattle. Watch the short-yardage run game and how Kansas City covers for Rice and Moore against a Seahawks team desperate to stop a two-game slide.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders chase a win after three straight losses

stories.text: Raiders try to stop a three-game slide
stories.summary: Las Vegas fell to 3-3 with a 33-30 home loss to Buffalo, its third straight defeat. Two of the three losses came by three points. The Rams visit Allegiant Stadium this afternoon.

stories.text: Thornton and Runyon out against the Rams
stories.summary: Receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) and tight end Carter Runyon (foot) are out. Running back Mike Washington Jr. (foot/back) is questionable. The Rams list receiver Puka Nacua (calf) as questionable.

stories.text: Tre Tucker scores twice against Buffalo
stories.summary: Tucker caught five passes for 97 yards and two touchdowns, one from 44 yards, and led the Raiders receivers in the loss. Kirk Cousins threw for 313 yards with two touchdowns and an interception on 23 of 41.

stories.text: 27.0: Raiders points per game, sixth in the NFL
stories.summary: Las Vegas scored 155 points through six games, the most since 2022, up from 14.3 per game and last in the league in 2025. Cousins has 14 touchdown passes, tied with Trevor Lawrence for the league lead.

stories.text: Rams at Raiders, Sunday 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Raiders host the Rams at Allegiant Stadium today. Watch whether the run game, 3.25 yards per carry against Buffalo, gives Cousins any help.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers use the bye to rethink everything

stories.text: Winless Chargers weigh changes during the bye
stories.summary: At 0-6, Jim Harbaugh said the staff is considering everything and may simplify the offense. The skid now covers eight games, counting the last two of 2025 and a wild-card loss to New England. The Chargers lost 22-6 to Kansas City last week.

stories.text: Alt, James and Harris targeted for Week 8
stories.summary: Tackle Joe Alt (neck) has missed two games, safety Derwin James (hamstring) three, and receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) is also out. The team hopes to have all three back after the bye. Center Tyler Biadasz is out for the season and Rashawn Slater is on injured reserve.

stories.text: Rookie Mesidor gives the defense a lift
stories.summary: Rookie edge rusher Akheem Mesidor has 2.5 sacks and a forced fumble. Fellow rookie Genesis Smith leads the team with two interceptions, and five rookies have played in all six games.

stories.text: 8: Justin Herbert's interceptions, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Herbert has 10 turnovers, a 59.4 percent completion rate against a 66.1 career mark, and has faced pressure on a league-high 99 dropbacks. The Chargers have taken 21 sacks, second most in the league.

stories.text: Bye now, Rams on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Los Angeles is off this week. The Rams (2-4) are the Week 8 opponent on Nov. 1, followed by Houston on Nov. 8. Watch the offensive line, which has started four rookies in recent games.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys face a must-win Monday night

stories.text: Prescott calls Eagles game a must-win for Dallas
stories.summary: Dak Prescott says the Cowboys have to go win Monday night after dropping two games they did not expect to lose. Dallas sits at 2-4 and has scored 16 and 13 points in its last two losses. ESPN still gives the Cowboys a 68 percent chance at the NFC East, because nobody in the division is pulling away.

stories.text: Turpin, Winters and Shelton out; Overshown set to return
stories.summary: The Cowboys ruled out receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs), linebacker Dee Winters (calf) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) for Monday. Linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) and safety P.J. Locke (foot) are questionable. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who has missed five games with a hamstring strain, is expected back, and cornerback Cobie Durant was trending toward a return as of Tuesday.

stories.text: Caleb Downs leads Dallas with 43 tackles
stories.summary: The rookie safety tops the Cowboys in tackles with 43 through six games. He plays on a defense that new coordinator Christian Parker is still fixing, with consultant Mike Pettine helping.

stories.text: 30th: where Dallas ranks in total defense
stories.summary: The Cowboys rank 30th in total defense and last against the run, giving up nearly 150 rushing yards a game. Philadelphia gets Saquon Barkley back from a hamstring injury, which makes that number the one to watch Monday.

stories.text: Eagles on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Dallas plays Philadelphia on Monday, October 26 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Watch whether the run defense holds up against Barkley and whether Overshown's return steadies the linebackers.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: McCarthy takes over at QB in Houston

stories.text: Harbaugh hands the offense to J.J. McCarthy
stories.summary: John Harbaugh benched Jameis Winston and named McCarthy the starter for the trip to Houston. Winston threw two interceptions in a loss to the Saints and has 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions as a starter. Jaxson Dart is out for the season with a knee injury.

stories.text: Edmunds, Holland and Johnson out against Houston
stories.summary: Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds went on reserve/injured with a shoulder injury, and safety Jevon Holland (concussion) and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were downgraded to out. Cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) is also out. Cornerback Paulson Adebo was activated from reserve.

stories.text: Malik Nabers piles up 12 catches for 165 yards
stories.summary: Nabers caught 12 passes for 165 yards against the Saints last Sunday. He also drew a career-high 20 targets in the Week 5 tie with Washington. He now has 168 career receptions.

stories.text: 957: Winston's passing yards as the Giants starter
stories.summary: Winston threw for 957 yards with seven touchdowns, five interceptions and a 57.0 completion percentage before Harbaugh made the change. He finished 14 of 26 for 152 yards against New Orleans. McCarthy came in and threw for 243 yards in relief.

stories.text: At Houston today, then the bye
stories.summary: The Giants play the Texans today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX, then go on their bye. Watch how McCarthy handles the first start of his Giants tenure and whether the run game, which has stalled, picks up.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles turn to McKee as Hurts is done

stories.text: Hurts out for the year with blood clots
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve after doctors found deep vein thrombosis and clots in both lungs, and he is expected to make a full recovery. Tanner McKee is set to start Monday night against Dallas. The Eagles are 2-4 after a 25-14 loss to Carolina.

stories.text: DeVonta Smith out, Barkley questionable
stories.summary: The Eagles ruled out receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), cornerback Michael Carter II (abdomen) and linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion). Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is questionable. Sources disagree on Smith's status, so check the final inactives.

stories.text: Tanner McKee faces the Cowboys with the keys
stories.summary: McKee went 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown against Carolina, a 77.5 passer rating behind an inexperienced offensive line. He is expected to start Monday.

stories.text: 0-6-2: the NFC East's combined record over two weeks
stories.summary: The division has gone winless over the last two weeks, with six losses and two ties. The Giants at 3-2-1 are the only team in the NFC East with a winning record.

stories.text: Cowboys on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Philadelphia faces Dallas on Monday, October 26 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Eagles have won three of the last four meetings. Watch Barkley's availability and how the line holds up.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders hit the bye with Quinn under fire

stories.text: Quinn's job talk follows the 49ers loss
stories.summary: Washington went into its bye at 1-4-1 and last in the NFC East after a 23-17 Monday night loss to San Francisco. Stephen A. Smith declared it over for Dan Quinn on First Take. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported a coaching change is not imminent and that Quinn still has the locker room.

stories.text: McLaurin lost for the season
stories.summary: Terry McLaurin tore a patellar tendon on Monday night and needs surgery, which ends his season, according to Athlon Sports. Stefon Diggs becomes the top receiver, with Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams in line for more work.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels throws for 300 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Daniels went 29 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns against San Francisco. Quinn also questioned his fourth-down throwaway in the second quarter, saying he should have taken a shot despite a flag on Washington.

stories.text: 303-90: the 49ers' first-half yardage edge
stories.summary: San Francisco outgained Washington 303 to 90 in the first half, led 20-3 and went 3 for 3 in the red zone. The Commanders went 0 for 4 on third down before the offense found a rhythm after halftime.

stories.text: Bye week, then the Eagles on November 1
stories.summary: Washington is on its bye this week. It returns Sunday, November 1 at 8:20 p.m. ET against Philadelphia, followed by the Rams on November 8.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears win a shootout, then lose Kmet

stories.text: Bears outlast Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Chicago won its second straight and moved to 5-2 by finishing the last quarter with the ball for more than 12 of 15 minutes. Rome Odunze recovered an onside kick with 37 seconds left to seal it. New England fell to 4-3 despite 321 passing yards from Drake Maye.

stories.text: Cole Kmet carted off with a knee injury
stories.summary: The tight end went down on a sideline catch in the fourth quarter Thursday. NFL Network reported the knee injury is likely season-ending, and ESPN reported he is headed to injured reserve. Testing could bring better news. Kmet, 27, is the longest-tenured Bear on the active roster. Running back Kyle Monangai was ruled out ahead of the game with thumb and toe injuries.

stories.text: Luther Burden III posts 130 yards in the first half
stories.summary: The receiver caught four passes for 130 yards and a 24-yard touchdown, all before halftime. Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards on 22 of 33 in his second game back from a hamstring injury. Reports differ on Williams' exact line, so check the box score before quoting it.

stories.text: 58: Cairo Santos' career-long field goal
stories.summary: Santos hit from 58 yards with 1:34 left, the longest kick of his career and the third longest in Soldier Field history. It gave Chicago a two-score lead. He had missed a 53-yarder earlier in the game.

stories.text: Bears head to Seattle on Monday night
stories.summary: Chicago plays at the Seahawks on Monday, Nov. 2, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN. The Bears will have to replace Kmet's snaps and find out whether Monangai is ready after missing a third straight game.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Rested Lions host Packers with a leaky secondary

stories.text: Lions come off the bye needing a defensive fix
stories.summary: Detroit sits 3-2 after losses to Buffalo and Carolina and a 45-21 win over Arizona. The offense ranks sixth in EPA per play, but the defense has been burned through five games. Dan Campbell called Green Bay an outstanding test and said the Lions must play cleaner and protect against deep throws.

stories.text: Kerby Joseph out, Branch and Mays questionable
stories.summary: Safety Kerby Joseph is out against Green Bay. Safety Brian Branch, center Cade Mays and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin are questionable. Campbell said barring a setback the Lions plan to play both Branch and Mays. Guard Ben Bartch, linebacker Devin White and receiver Tom Kennedy are on injured reserve.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs carries the Lions' offense
stories.summary: Gibbs has 504 rushing yards on 105 carries, 4.8 per attempt, with seven touchdowns through five games. He also catches the ball out of the backfield, which makes him the first player Green Bay has to account for.

stories.text: 12-0: Goff's touchdown to interception ratio
stories.summary: Jared Goff has thrown 12 touchdown passes and no interceptions through five games. He threw for 271 yards, three touchdowns and ran for another score in the win over Arizona.

stories.text: Packers visit Ford Field this afternoon
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Green Bay today at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, its first game since the bye. Watch whether the front four can push Jordan Love off his spot, which Campbell called the key to the game.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers ride a three-game streak into Detroit

stories.text: Packers beat Dallas 23-13 for a third straight win
stories.summary: Green Bay led 17-0 at halftime, the first time Dallas was shut out in a first half since November 2021. The Packers are 4-2 and have won 11 of their last 13 meetings with the Cowboys, with one tie. Running back Josh Jacobs, who has not played this season, was set to come off the commissioner's exempt list the Monday after the game.

stories.text: Jordan Love fights through a sore back
stories.summary: Love took hard hits against Dallas and was limited in Wednesday's practice. Matt LaFleur said he was pretty beat up, and Love has said he will play. Cornerbacks Benjamin St-Juste and Brandon Cisse and guard Aaron Banks are questionable, and edge rusher Micah Parsons remains on PUP-R.

stories.text: Matthew Golden gets 104 yards and a touchdown
stories.summary: The receiver caught six passes for 104 yards and a 9-yard score that finished a 90-yard opening drive. He also dropped a 43-yard touchdown. Love went 23 of 41 for 276 yards and added a 1-yard sneak for a score.

stories.text: 7: Packers interceptions, the most in the NFL
stories.summary: Green Bay's defense leads the league in picks. Evan Williams and rookie Brandon Cisse each intercepted Dak Prescott on Sunday night, and Cisse's was the first of his career.

stories.text: Packers at Lions today on FOX
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at Detroit at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The Packers carry a three-game winning streak into Ford Field and need Love healthy against a Lions defense that has given up big plays.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings get Jordan Mason back

stories.text: Vikings activate Jordan Mason before the Colts game
stories.summary: Minnesota, 5-0 and fresh off a Week 6 bye, activated the running back on Saturday after a Week 1 hand surgery. The team cut DeeJay Dallas to open the roster spot, then re-signed him to the practice squad. Mason ran 15 times for 59 yards and a score in the 39-22 opener against Green Bay.

stories.text: Vikings enter Colts game nearly healthy
stories.summary: Mason was the only Viking carrying a designation on the final report, listed as questionable with a thumb issue. Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson had no designation after full practices. Christian Darrisaw sat out Friday as a veteran rest day. Indianapolis is without cornerback Sauce Gardner, tight end Tyler Warren and receiver Anthony Gould.

stories.text: Aaron Jones has carried the backfield
stories.summary: With Mason sidelined, Jones piled up 85 carries for 370 yards since Week 2. He now shares the load again.

stories.text: 34: Will Reichard's consecutive field goals
stories.summary: Reichard has made all 15 of his attempts this season and 34 in a row dating to last year. He faces Colts kicker Spencer Shrader, who is 18 for 18, in what Bring Me The Sports called a kicker duel.

stories.text: Colts visit U.S. Bank Stadium for a 1 p.m. kickoff
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Indianapolis today at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, going for 6-0. The Colts are 2-4 after losing to Tennessee, and the Vikings lead the league's turnover margin tied at plus 6 while Indianapolis is last at minus 8.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons seek a first home win against 49ers

stories.text: Falcons fall to 0-3 at home after another slow start
stories.summary: Chicago ran out to a 31-7 lead before Atlanta rallied in the fourth quarter and lost 31-23. Rookie Zachariah Branch muffed a punt and fumbled a kickoff, and Michael Penix Jr. lost a fumble on a late sack that ended the comeback. Kevin Stefanski put the slow start on himself and his staff.

stories.text: Brian Robinson, Divine Deablo out; A.J. Terrell questionable
stories.summary: Atlanta ruled out running back Brian Robinson (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm), defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and tackle Michael Jerrell (biceps) for the 49ers. Cornerback A.J. Terrell, back from injured reserve, practiced fully Friday and is questionable with a groin issue, as is end Za'Darius Smith (neck).

stories.text: Bijan Robinson leads the NFL in scrimmage yards
stories.summary: Robinson has 758 yards from scrimmage, 641 of them on the ground, tops in the league. With Brian Robinson out, he should carry the backfield load against a 49ers front that has already piled up 15 sacks.

stories.text: 9: times Penix has been sacked in four games
stories.summary: The 49ers have 15 sacks through six games after finishing with a league-low 20 all of last season. Penix is 2-2 as a starter, and the matchup that matters sits on his right side, where Atlanta's tackle and guard face San Francisco's left-side pass rushers.

stories.text: Atlanta hosts unbeaten San Francisco today at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The 49ers (6-0) visit Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Fox. Raheem Morris, fired as Falcons coach in January, now runs the San Francisco defense. Atlanta has lost all three home games and needs clean special teams to stay in this one.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers lead the South and host Tampa Bay

stories.text: Panthers take the division lead with a win in Philadelphia
stories.summary: Carolina beat the Eagles 25-14 on Sunday to reach 3-2. Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns, both to Tommy Tremble, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards. The Panthers took 13 penalties for 149 yards and still pulled away.

stories.text: Phillips, Incoom out; Freeling questionable for Tampa Bay
stories.summary: Edge rushers Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Thomas Incoom (calf) are out. Tackle Monroe Freeling (knee) and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) are questionable. Young practiced fully all week with a knee listing.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard keeps finding the end zone
stories.summary: Hubbard has 426 rushing yards and six touchdowns, and he piled up 120 yards in Philadelphia, including a 19-yard run on fourth-and-1 that kept a drive alive. He closed that game with a 2-yard touchdown run.

stories.text: 2nd: Carolina's rank in total offense
stories.summary: The Panthers average 404.4 yards a game, second in the NFL, after ranking 27th last year. Young leads the league at 309.8 passing yards per game. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik took over play-calling from coach Dave Canales.

stories.text: Panthers host Tampa Bay today at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Carolina meets a Bucs team that is 1-5 and has Baker Mayfield questionable with a thumb injury. Tampa Bay has won 10 of the last 12 meetings. Watch whether the Panthers' 25th-ranked total defense can hold up against the league's second-ranked rushing defense on the other side.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints open Paris game under owner pressure

stories.text: Saints play the NFL's first Paris game with Benson watching
stories.summary: New Orleans (2-4) faces Pittsburgh at Stade de France at 9:30 a.m. ET. Owner Gayle Benson said last week that the team's performance is not acceptable, which puts heat on coach Kellen Moore and GM Mickey Loomis. A win over the Giants last Sunday gave the Saints a pulse.

stories.text: Ruiz and Shepherd questionable for Paris
stories.summary: Right guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) was limited Friday, and rookie Jeremiah Wright would start if he can't go. Defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) missed Friday and the previous two games. Linebacker Kaden Elliss and end Anfernee Jennings are back after three weeks out, and kicker Daniel Carlson flew in Friday while waiting on the birth of his child.

stories.text: Alvin Kamara joins an exclusive 5,000-5,000 club
stories.summary: Kamara caught a 31-yard touchdown against the Giants and became the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000 career rushing and receiving yards. It was his 90th career touchdown, a franchise record. He still carries a back issue into Paris but has no game designation.

stories.text: 828: rushing yards the Saints have allowed
stories.summary: New Orleans ranks 30th in rushing yards allowed and 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed (11) through six games. Pittsburgh brings a run game that can lean on that weakness.

stories.text: Bye week follows the Steelers game
stories.summary: Today's kickoff is 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. A loss would leave the Saints 2-5 heading into the bye, and Tyler Shough's turnovers, eight giveaways so far, remain the thing to watch.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs try to stop the slide in Charlotte

stories.text: Bucs blow a 16-3 lead and lose in overtime
stories.summary: Pittsburgh scored on five straight possessions, Chase McLaughlin forced overtime with a 53-yard field goal, and Aaron Rodgers hit Germie Bernard for the winning touchdown in a 26-19 final. Tampa Bay is 1-5. Todd Bowles said the team has no margin for error.

stories.text: Mayfield questionable; Egbuka, Goedeke, Winfield out
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield practiced fully all week with his dislocated right thumb and is questionable after missing three games. Receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion, foot), tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ribs) are out. If Mayfield sits, rookie Jalon Daniels makes a fourth start.

stories.text: David Walker has become the pass rush
stories.summary: Walker had two sacks against Pittsburgh and leads Tampa Bay with 4.0. Two more today would make him the first Buccaneer since Jason Pierre-Paul with consecutive multi-sack games.

stories.text: 6 of 19: Tampa Bay's third-down conversions vs. Pittsburgh
stories.summary: The offense managed 224 yards and Bucky Irving gained 46 on 19 carries. The defense had a season-high five sacks, but the offense could not finish drives or hold the lead.

stories.text: Bucs visit Carolina today at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Panthers (3-2) lead the NFC South. Tampa Bay has the league's second-ranked rushing defense (75.5 yards a game) and will test Carolina's 27th-ranked run defense with Irving.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Cardinals honor Fitzgerald, minus four starters

stories.text: Fitzgerald gets his Ring of Honor day against Denver
stories.summary: Larry Fitzgerald goes into the Cardinals Ring of Honor at State Farm Stadium today, before the Broncos game. He says the date was planned about three years ago, and he picked this week because it falls in Breast Cancer Awareness Month and his son Devin has a bye at Notre Dame. Arizona sits at 2-4 and wants to send the crowd home happy.

stories.text: Love, Nolen, Wingard and Gaines are out
stories.summary: Running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle), defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle), safety Andrew Wingard (knee) and guard Jon Gaines (knee) will not play. Quarterback Carson Beck (back), safety Budda Baker (groin, illness), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and lineman Darius Robinson (back) are questionable. Hayden Conner steps in at right guard, and the team sees Baker improving.

stories.text: Ryland wins NFC special teams honor for six-kick day
stories.summary: Kicker Chad Ryland made all six field goal tries in the 18-16 win at the Rams, from 34, 30, 22, 38, 27 and 43 yards. He scored every Arizona point, and the 43-yarder won it as time expired. The NFL named him NFC Special Teams Player of the Week, his first.

stories.text: 14: Ryland's field goals, tied for third in the NFL
stories.summary: Ryland has made 14 field goals this season, tied for third in the league. His 54 points rank fourth. Six of those kicks came last Sunday, the most by anyone in a single game this year.

stories.text: Broncos at State Farm Stadium, today, 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona hosts Denver (4-2) this afternoon on CBS. Inactives come out 90 minutes before kickoff, and the Cardinals are watching the Beck, Baker, Melton and Robinson statuses. Watch how the offense moves without Love in the backfield.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams limp to Vegas short on receivers

stories.text: Rams drop 18-16 to Arizona and sit last in the NFC West
stories.summary: The Rams lost at SoFi Stadium last Sunday on a Chad Ryland field goal as time expired. They lead the league with 644 yards over six games but keep stalling before the end zone. Arizona held the ball for nearly 35 minutes, and Tyler Higbee fumbled in the red zone.

stories.text: Adams ruptured a hamstring, Ford is done for the year
stories.summary: Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring in the final minute against Arizona and could miss six to 10 weeks. Kobie Turner (groin) is headed to injured reserve, and nose tackle Poona Ford is out for the season. Kicker Blake Grupe is also on IR. For today, Puka Nacua (calf) and Trent McDuffie (groin) are questionable, and Nate Landman is out with a concussion.

stories.text: Stafford carries the passing game with 299 yards a week
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford averages 299.0 passing yards per game, but he has thrown six interceptions. With Adams down, Nacua is the only proven receiver on the roster until Terrance Ferguson returns. Stafford will need to find answers beyond one target.

stories.text: 644: yards the Rams have piled up, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Los Angeles leads the league with 644 yards through six games, yet it is 2-4. Against Arizona it managed 16 points and went home with a loss. The yards are there. The points are not.

stories.text: At Raiders, today, 4:25 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Rams visit Allegiant Stadium to face Las Vegas (3-3). Watch who lines up opposite Nacua with Adams gone, and whether a defense missing Turner and Ford can slow the Raiders on the ground.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Unbeaten 49ers fly east without Evans and Bosa

stories.text: 49ers go for 7-0 in Atlanta on a short week
stories.summary: San Francisco is 6-0 after a 23-17 win over Washington on Monday night, and it now travels cross-country with six days between games. Mike Evans aggravated his Achilles in that game and is out. The 49ers have a bye after this one.

stories.text: Six ruled out, including Evans, Bosa and Samuel
stories.summary: Evans (Achilles), Nick Bosa (calf), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Marques Sigle (ankle), Garret Wallow (hamstring) and Luke Gifford (groin) are all out. Bosa misses his fifth straight game, and Kyle Shanahan said he still felt soreness. Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and newly signed Brandin Cooks are the receivers left.

stories.text: Kittle quietly on pace for another 1,000 yards
stories.summary: George Kittle has 338 receiving yards and five touchdowns through six games, eight months after his Achilles injury. He passed Vernon Davis as the franchise leader in tight end receiving touchdowns. He is on pace for a fifth 1,000-yard season.

stories.text: 57: Kittle's receiving touchdowns, a 49ers tight end record
stories.summary: Kittle has 57 career receiving touchdowns, the most ever by a 49ers tight end. Gene Washington is next on the franchise list at 59, which puts third place two touchdowns away.

stories.text: At Falcons, today, 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: San Francisco plays at Mercedes-Benz Stadium against Atlanta (2-4). Watch how the receiver room handles Evans and Samuel being out, and whether the pass rush holds up without Bosa. The bye follows.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks need a win and a clean Darnold night

stories.text: Seahawks fell 17-14 in overtime to Denver on Thursday
stories.summary: Seattle lost at Denver on October 15 when Sam Darnold threw an interception on the first overtime drive, setting up Will Lutz's 53-yard field goal. Jason Myers had forced overtime with a 34-yarder with three seconds left. The defending champions arrive at Sunday night's game at 3-3.

stories.text: Charbonnet out again, Lock questionable with elbow
stories.summary: Running back Zach Charbonnet will not make his season debut. He is coming back from a torn ACL, and Mike Macdonald called it part of the plan with no setback. Linebackers Drake Thomas and Chazz Surratt are out. Quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow), safety Nick Emmanwori (hip) and linebackers Uchenna Nwosu, DeMarcus Lawrence and Connor O'Toole are questionable.

stories.text: Smith-Njigba caught 12 passes for 134 in the loss
stories.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba led Seattle with 12 receptions and 134 yards at Denver. The offense piled up 353 yards but turned the ball over three times. He remains the most reliable target in the building.

stories.text: 7: Darnold's interceptions this season
stories.summary: Darnold has thrown seven interceptions in 2026, half of his 2025 total, and he threw two against Denver while going 27 of 51 for 278 yards with no touchdowns. He was sacked at least five times.

stories.text: Chiefs at Lumen Field, tonight, 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Seattle hosts undefeated Kansas City (5-0) on Sunday Night Football. Watch the pass protection, the Lock elbow status and the linebacker rotation. Sources list kickoff at 8:15 or 8:20; NFL.com says 8:20.
